_doc: The journal: the armoury's JOURNAL tab (the owner's armoury reference: 'a journal of what was learned'). Sections, then entries; an entry is shown once its 'unlock' key is learned (none or 'start': from the first moment). Keys (SOJournal.h): met:<species> (one was killed where the player was), named:<variant> (a named one), stage:<operation>:<stage> (a stage of an operation began), done:<operation> (finished), origin:<origin> (a gun of that maker came in). An operation's own pages (its briefing, the radio as each stage begins, its outcome) are not written here: they are read from its plan (Data/areas.json). 'picture': /Game/UI/Journal/T_Journal_<picture> (tools/blender/skr/lab.py --portraits, SO_IMPORT_ONLY=journal). 'tally': a count shown with it (kill:<species> = how many this player has killed). Our own words; nothing of the war has a date or a length of time.

sections.name: The Sarketh
sections.line: What their dead have taught us

sections.name: Operations
sections.line: Briefings and what the radio said

entries.title: The Sarketh
entries.text:
One people, built much as we are and of a size with us. What makes one of them small and quick and another a wall of metal is what he was issued.

The force on Meridian came down after the station and has been cut off since the fleet left. What it has is what it landed with, and that goes by rank: a foot soldier gets a light gun and little else; the higher the command, the more armour and the bigger the gun, up to powered armour and, for the one who commands the garrison, a walking war suit.

Every one of them carries a gun. Their light guns are the pattern ours were copied from.

They want Sol, for the Sarketh. So does every other people the empire left here, which is why they fight each other before they fight us.

entries.title: Levy
entries.text:
The many. A Levy is issued light armour, a light automatic gun and very little else, and there are always more of them.

Levies come on in numbers and keep coming, from cover to cover. They are how the Sarketh find out where you are.

Their plates are left as they came from the forge: grey, unmarked.
entries.note: Light armour, a light automatic gun. Numbers.

entries.title: Veteran
entries.text:
Full armour and a rifle, and the sense to use both. Veterans take cover, work round a flank and fall back when a fight turns against them.

They are the backbone of the garrison. Where a Levy pushes, a Veteran waits for you to show yourself.

Their plates are finished in a cold steel blue.
entries.note: Full armour, a rifle. Cover, flanks, a fighting withdrawal.

entries.title: Speaker
entries.text:
The Speakers carry the crystal sets that talk to the command net, a marksman's rifle, and a cloak that hides them for a step.

What a Speaker sees, the rest know. They fire from far back and do not stay where they were seen.

Their lacquer is a deep teal, the colour of the net.
entries.note: A marksman's rifle, the net's crystal set, a cloak for a step.

entries.title: Runner
entries.text:
Runners are issued almost nothing: a blade and the speed to use it. They move in groups and close the distance before you have counted them.

A pack holds off until enough of it is in place, then goes in together. Cut two of them down quickly and the rest break off.

Their plates are sand-coloured, the colour of the ground they cross.
entries.note: Almost nothing issued. Speed, and the pack.

entries.title: Warden
entries.text:
An officer's suit: powered armour a head taller than a soldier, a shield along one arm and a gun for close work.

The shield turns what hits it, but what it turns still shakes the one inside. Hammer the plate and it comes down while he reels.

Wardens hold the gates. Their plates are finished in ivory and gold.
entries.note: Powered armour, a shield, a gun for close work.

entries.title: Bearer
entries.text:
The same suit as a Warden's, built round a gun too heavy to carry without it, and the drum that feeds it.

A Bearer does not take cover. It sets itself and keeps a place under fire until whatever was there stops moving. Its plates turn half of what comes from the front.

Its plates are bronze.
entries.note: Powered armour round a heavy gun and its feed.

entries.title: The Commander
entries.text:
The one who commands Meridian does not fight on foot. He walks in a war suit with the garrison's heaviest weapons, and he had not left the Crown since the day they landed.

The suit is shielded for as long as what feeds it lives. Stop the feed and it staggers.

Its plates are lacquered crimson. Nothing else on Meridian wears that colour.
entries.note: A walking war suit, the garrison's heaviest weapons.

entries.title: The Gatekeeper
entries.text:
One Warden kept the Galleria's service gate shut through everything that came against it. His suit is older than the others', and has been mended more often.

He is not holding the gate any more.

entries.title: Levy Captain
entries.text:
Levies under a captain fight harder and move faster: he calls them on, and they hear it.

When a captain falls, those round him falter. The ones who learned that early learned to look for the captain first.

entries.title: Senior Speaker
entries.text:
The senior Speakers carry a heavier set. Its pulse goes through what we carry: for a while after it, nothing you have but your gun will answer.

The pulse takes a moment to build. You can see it coming.

entries.title: Lead Runner
entries.text:
A pack has one it follows. It calls, and the pack comes in round it.

It is faster than the rest, and it knows where you are going to be.

entries.title: Veteran Hunter
entries.text:
Some Veterans are sent after one target and nothing else. They close with a lunge, and they throw charges into the cover you are using.

The one in the Concord Ring was waiting for us.

entries.title: Speaker Marksman
entries.sub: A SPEAKER WITH A LONG GUN
entries.text:
A line of light on you is a Marksman taking aim. When the line holds still, the shot comes a breath later.

They watch the Sluice from the footbridges, and they move after every few shots.

entries.title: Warden Gunner
entries.sub: A WARDEN WITH A HEAVIER GUN
entries.text: A Warden issued a gun meant for a Bearer, and the suit to carry it. It keeps the shield.

entries.title: The Spread
entries.text:
Humanity had spread through its own system: stations round Earth, cities on the Moon and on Mars, outposts as far as the outer moons.

It was the furthest we had ever gone, and we thought it was ours.

entries.title: The Vanthos Empire
entries.text:
Many peoples under one throne, each with its own worlds, its own fleets and its own lords. They did not like each other. The throne was the one thing they all obeyed.

It came in from the edge of the system with all of them.

entries.title: The Long Retreat
entries.text:
We met the empire at the edge of the system and lost. It came inward a world at a time: the outer moons, the belt, Mars, the Moon.

We lost each one more slowly than the last, until the fight was in the sky over Earth and the ring of stations round the planet was breaking.

entries.title: The Turn
entries.text:
Then the empire's ships began firing on each other. Destroyers rammed freighters. Landing columns turned their guns on the column beside them. Nobody on Earth understood what they were seeing.

Most of the fleet pulled out of the system, still fighting itself as it went. We hit what we could reach as it left. Some of it never got away.

entries.title: Those Who Stayed
entries.text:
What stayed behind is still here: on Earth, in the wreck of the orbit and on every world they took from us. They are not one army any more. Each people holds the ground it was standing on and means to have the whole system for its own.

A place held by one of them has only that people in it. They fight their neighbours for Sol, and that is the only reason we are still alive.

entries.title: Shattered Orbit
entries.text:
The broken ring of stations and the hulks of the fleet that died there are still overhead. On a clear night you can watch them turn.

Some of them came down. Meridian was under one.

entries.title: Nexus Prime
entries.text:
The first city rebuilt, raised round a grounded carrier of theirs whose heart still runs. It powers the city.

Shields, light guns and the first new ships of our own come out of it.

entries.title: Orion
entries.text:
Small teams carrying the best of the stolen technology, sent into the places still held to kill what holds them and bring back what works.

You are one of them.

entries.title: The Rampart Directorate
entries.text:
The command that holds what has been retaken. Rampart sends the teams in, and Rampart's is the voice you hear on the way.

It does not tell you how to fight. It tells you what the place was.

entries.title: The Institute
entries.sub: THE PEOPLE WHO TAKE THEM APART
entries.text:
The Institute takes the empire's machines apart. Everything the city has came out of its workshops.

So did the mistakes that cost it districts. The annex on the Sluice was one of theirs.

entries.title: Void Crystal
entries.sub: WHAT THEIR MACHINES ARE GROWN FROM
entries.text:
Power, memory and armour in one material. Every people of the empire used it; none of them made it. Their machines are grown from it, not built.

Everything we have learned, we learned by cutting it open.

entries.title: What Earth Fears
entries.text:
That when one of them has won whatever they are fighting for out there, it will come back.

The Sarketh on Meridian were calling for theirs. Nothing answered. Nobody here knows why.

entries.title: Nexus Prime Steel
entries.text:
Ballistic guns from the city's own workshops: steel, brass and powder, made the way guns were made before the empire came.

They are heavy, loud and honest. A round leaves the barrel faster than any bolt of light and drops on its way to the target.

entries.title: Institute Light Guns
entries.text:
Built on Sarketh patterns taken off the dead. They fire plasma: a bolt you can watch fly, so lead what moves.

They reload their own way. Some take a fresh cell, some throw their heat out through a vent, and some open and draw energy in from the air.

entries.title: Sarketh Make
entries.text:
Their own guns. They fire crystalline slugs that go on through what they hit, and they are never reloaded: rest the trigger and the crystal condenses new rounds out of the reserve.

Fire too long and the crystal heats, then faster, then it vents whether you want it to or not.

entries.title: Grown
entries.text:
Living weapons: grown, not made. They feed, and they spit what they make of it.

Nobody is sure they are only weapons.

entries.title: Void Requiem
entries.text:
Made by a people no human has met. They are not Sarketh work.

Where they came from is a question the Institute would like answered.

entries.title: Service Record
entries.text: What you have done since you joined Orion, as the Directorate keeps it.
